reviewer: Independent AI tester: Gateway-graduate Runner perspective
method: Actual shared-browser incognito tab, rendered DOM button clicks and input/change events. Public localTable snapshots only during play. Routine actions used a bounded public-information heuristic driver, with manual opening choice and adjustments. No engine choices injected, hidden cards inspected, source edits, headless browser, or claims of human novice evidence. No screenshot-based visual audit performed.

guideChoice.reason: Familiar identities and a small new-card package; fit the guide's first-Vantage learning path.

crafting.name: Panel Runner 19Nov
crafting.rationale: Focus on the named Tailor learning goal by increasing the probability of drawing it; remove a conditional out-of-faction resource. The second Tailor is unique and can be a dead duplicate, an explicit consistency tradeoff. This was a test hypothesis, not an optimization claim.
crafting.ui: Tune deck opened from selected list, counted +/- changes live, showed40cards7/15 influence and Ready to play, and Save & use selected the local list. Game embedded the exact custom document.
crafting.limitation: Guide gives pairing/learning goals but no candidate swaps, package dependencies, copy-count advice, or explanation of which benchmark observations still apply after changes.

ratings.scale: Subjective AI tester impressions out of10, based on one full game; not aggregate human ratings.

worked: The separate learning paths made the next goal concrete without changing identity.
Runner-win direction, sample counts, and preliminary labels were unambiguous.
The guide explicitly says custom decks are not benchmarked; important after tuning.
Changes summary, faction/influence totals and Save & use made one legal swap straightforward.
Tailor installed during game; weakened ice was visible, including Tithe at0 strength. Full game reached terminal with no diagnostic.

findings.finding: Guide helps select a list but barely helps craft one.
findings.evidence: Its concrete advice is a named deck/pairing and a card to learn; to decide an actual swap I supplied my own understanding of uniqueness, conditional resources and consistency.
findings.recommendation: Add a small 'Try one change' recipe for each learning path: suggested cut/add, why, legal totals, expected tradeoff, and dependency warning.

findings.finding: Learning goal is not translated into a turn-by-turn plan.
findings.evidence: I installed Tailor but attacked HQ before completing my breaker rig, took repeated net damage and lost0–7. Driver choice is the main confound, but the guide did not supply a starting-hand checklist or first-run safety prompts.
findings.recommendation: Add compact mulligan priorities, minimum grip against damage, breaker/economy setup, and what to watch when the lesson triggers.

findings.finding: Guide-to-lobby handoff requires remembering exact deck names.
findings.evidence: I read the recommended pairing, clicked Back to lobby, then separately chose Runner and Corp in dropdowns. There is no Use this pairing action.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit Use this pairing links which populate both selected lists and preserve the return path, without auto-starting a game.

findings.finding: The page remains Runner-centric for opponent exploration.
findings.evidence: The only perspective selector is Your Runner deck and results always use Runner percentages. This was clear for my role, but does not directly help a Corp player choose an opponent.
findings.recommendation: Allow Corp perspective with explicit win-rate direction.

findings.finding: Vantage card inspector provenance is mislabeled.
findings.evidence: After the game I clicked installed The Tungsten Tailor. Rules/title were correct but the inspector footer said 'Art by Si F Sweetman · System Gateway #3'.
findings.recommendation: Use the actual expansion name from card metadata in inspector attribution.

gameplayNotes: The first hand had Sure Gamble,Overclock,Cleaver,Jailbreak,Cleaver; kept because it provided income plus an initial breaker.
Tailor came online early, so the swap's learning target was actually seen.

The bounded driver overvalued HQ events and setup; it hit Diviner/Tithe before a complete rig, then became conservative about raw runs. This is a testing-policy weakness, not a demonstrated balance defect.
Corp scored7points in round9. The guide's52% describes AI averages for the original list; this one custom-list loss does not contradict it.
No blocked installation, endless mandatory paid ability, missing Keep button or crash was observed.
overall: Useful as a next-matchup chooser and learning syllabus; incomplete as a deck-crafting guide. The deckbuilder itself made the legal one-card experiment easy.
